items.title: Headlines for November 17, 2026 | Democracy Now!
items.excerpt: ## Trump Arrives in Philippines Ahead of ASEAN Summit and Meeting with Putin, Xi Nov 17, 2026 President Trump has arrived in the Philippines on the first leg of a 48-hour trip to Asia. Trump landed in Manila aboard the new Air Force One, a luxury 747 jet gifted to him by the government of Qatar. He’s scheduled to meet with President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. ahead of the ASEAN summit of Southeast Asian nations. Trump’s visit has drawn large protests in Manila, where police arrested hundreds of people over the weekend. Students, workers and progressive groups are demanding an end to the U.S. and Israeli war on Iran and are protesting against plans to build an artificial intelligence and manufacturing hub near Manila. On Thursday, Trump will hold an unprecedented trilateral summit in Shenzhen, China, with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin. Trump also said he might meet with North Korean leader Kim Jong-un while in China. ## Trump Says He “Would Not Mind” Seeing Jensen Huang Restored as CEO of Nvidia Nov 17, 2026 The Trump administration said Monday it would investigate Megaspeed, the Singapore-based cloud computing firm that’s accused of sending advanced Nvidia computer chips to China, in violation of U.S. export controls. The investigation follows Nvidia founder Jensen Huang’s resignation as CEO, after he admitted he’d had an extramarital affair with former Megaspeed executive Alice Huang. Megaspeed said on Sunday she had left the company more than a year ago. On Monday, President Trump responded to reports that Jensen Huang is in discussions with allies about a potential return to Nvidia. > Reporter: “Mr. President, do you want to see Jensen Huang reinstated as CEO of Nvidia?” > President Donald Trump: “I would — I would not mind. I would not mind that. I like — you know, I threw out the name of Tim Cook. But I would say that the — Jensen’s reinstatement, I think he learned a big lesson, I guess maybe one lesson more important than another. But I would certainly not mind seeing that.” ## Trump Takes “No Responsibility” for Largest FAA Ground Stop Since 9/11 Nov 17, 2026 United Airlines canceled dozens of departing flights and delayed more than 800 others on Monday after a system outage that lasted more than 90 minutes. United blamed a “technical issue,” without elaborating, and said in a statement there was “no indication that this was a cybersecurity-related issue.” This comes after the FAA ordered a nearly five-hour nationwide ground stop on Friday, causing over 18,000 flight cancellations and more than 28,000 delays. It was the largest disruption of its kind to U.S. air travel since the 9/11 attacks. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy is due to brief senators about the incident today. On Monday, President Trump said Duffy had his full support, and blamed the Biden administration for the grounded flights. > President Donald Trump: “I don’t take any responsibility. They did a great job. Secretary Duffy, they acted incredibly. Everybody was safe. Nobody was hurt. No crashes, no nothing.” Shortly after taking office in January 2025, Trump signed an executive order freezing the remaining funds in a $25 billion Biden-era appropriation to modernize flight infrastructure. ... ## Israel Failed to Meet Commitments to Deliver Food and Supplies to Gaza Nov 17, 2026 In Gaza, Israeli forces killed a young Palestinian man and wounded others in an attack east of the city of Deir al-Balah in central Gaza. Elsewhere, Israeli forces killed one Palestinian and injured five in the north, while in southern Gaza, Israeli forces shot and wounded three Palestinians, including a child, inside a school. The latest killings come as Israel has failed to meet its aid commitments under the Gaza ceasefire deal. Data obtained by Haaretz showed decreasing food deliveries to Gaza, alongside severe shortages of medical supplies, tents and materials to repair damaged infrastructure. The U.N. is also urging the protection of aid workers and hospitals. This is U.N. spokesperson Farhan Haq. > Farhan Haq: “Yesterday, an Israeli airstrike hit very close to a U.N.-led fuel convoy in Rafah. We are concerned that strikes at targets near our staff and vehicles, especially vehicles carrying fuel, expose them to unacceptable risks. Civilians, including humanitarian workers, must always be protected.” ## Israeli Opposition Slams Netanyahu’s “Attempted Coup” over Framed Arab MKs Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is facing scrutiny after he claimed Israel’s October 27 election was stolen. Now there are new allegations that his administration interfered in the election. An investigation by Israel’s Channel 12 reported that Netanyahu aides gave police tips shortly before the vote, which led to Arab party workers being arrested on Election Day. The report also said the Shin Bet chief, whom Netanyahu personally appointed, tried to wiretap five Arab members of parliament. Following the report, the head of the opposition, Gadi Eisenkot, said, “Under no circumstances can Netanyahu remain at the helm of government for even one more minute. Under no circumstances must Israel be dragged into another election with him as prime minister.” Netanyahu had been pressuring Eisenkot to form a unity government with his right-wing Likud party. ## Iran Attacks U.S. Radar Station in Bahrain, Says It Captured U.S. Drone Nov 17, 2026 Bahrain’s military says it intercepted an Iranian drone strike targeting a U.S. radar facility — the third attack of its kind in recent days. The assault came after U.S. Central Command announced a third carrier strike group, the USS Theodore Roosevelt, had arrived in the Middle East, adding about 10,000 sailors and Marines to U.S. forces in the region. Meanwhile, Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps says it had hacked the flight guidance system of a U.S.-made MQM-170 drone and landed it remotely, intact. It’s the latest in a series of similar claims by Iran. Meanwhile, three more vessels caught fire while transiting the Strait of Hormuz today, including a ship carrying liquefied natural gas and a supertanker holding more than 2 million barrels of crude oil. ## Ukrainian Strike Damages Bridge Linking Crimea to Russia Russia reports that Ukraine has carried out its largest drone strike of the war so far. According to Moscow, the attack damaged the major bridge connecting Russia with occupied Crimea and struck several oil refineries. Russian officials say their forces shot down over 2,000 drones and four long-range Flamingo missiles in a 24-hour period. Moscow’s mayor said about 600 of those drones were aimed at the capital. Meanwhile, Kyiv had 17 air raid alerts in one day, the most on record. Russian strikes killed at least seven people in Ukraine, as attacks on energy infrastructure left 50,000 people without power.

items.title: Fed’s Musalem: US likely needs several rate hikes by spring to control inflation By Reuters
items.excerpt: WASHINGTON, Nov 17 (Reuters) - The US Federal Reserve many need several rate hikes to bring high inflation under control and should act soon to ensure the problem doesn’t get worse, St. Louis Fed president Alberto Musalem said on Tuesday. "The economy will likely require several interest rate increases before the spring of 2027 to achieve price stability in a timely manner," Musalem said, arguing that the current policy rate, in the 3.75% to 4% range, is as much as a percentage point below where it needs to be to return inflation to the Fed’s 2% target. It is currently running above 3%, and Musalem said the most likely scenario is that it remains elevated unless the Fed acts. The Fed next meets on Dec. 8-9 and is expected to approve a quarter percentage point rate hike. Musalem is not a voter on interest rate policy this year. "Inflation is too high...Looking ahead, risks are skewed toward persistent above-target inflation," with current policy not acting as significant restraint on growth that continues above trend, Musalem said in remarks prepared for delivery to a Central Bank of Argentina conference in Buenos Aires. "Moving sooner, while inflation expectations are anchored, has a better chance of succeeding without adverse impact on the labor market or economic growth," he said.

items.title: US import prices rise more than expected in October By Reuters
items.excerpt: WASHINGTON, Nov 17 (Reuters) - US import prices increased more than expected in October, the latest indication that inflation pressures were broadening beyond energy goods. Import prices advanced 1.1% last month after rising by the same margin in September, the Labor Department’s Bureau of Labor Statistics said on Tuesday. Economists polled by Reuters had forecast import prices, which exclude tariffs, climbing 0.7%. The BLS did not publish year-over-year import price readings because last year’s federal government shutdown prevented the collection of data in October 2025, leaving no comparison base. Imported inflation accelerated 8.1% in September, the largest gain in just more than four years. The government last week reported stronger-than-expected consumer prices in October as well as firmer producer inflation details, reinforcing economists’ views inflation was broadening beyond the energy sector as the US-Israeli war with Iran drags on. Economists expect the Federal Reserve to continue raising interest rates after next month’s widely expected hike. ... Import prices were last month driven by a 3.6% rise in the cost of fuels. That followed a 6.3% jump in September. There were also increases in the prices of petroleum and natural gas. Imported food prices fell 0.2% after rising 0.4% in September. Excluding the fuels and food, import prices shot up 0.9% after increasing 0.5% in September. Prices of imported capital goods soared 1.5%, driven by a 1.7% jump in the cost of nonelectrical machinery. That is likely related to the AI infrastructure buildout. Imported capital goods prices advanced 1.0% in September. Imported automotive vehicles, parts and engines prices increased 0.4% after gaining 0.3% in September. Prices for consumer goods, excluding automotives, rose 0.5% after climbing 0.3% in September.

items.title: Citi sees early signs of energy pass through By Investing.com
items.excerpt: Investing.com -- Citi told clients in a note Tuesday that October’s consumer price data may offer the clearest signs yet that higher energy and transport costs are filtering through to other prices, though it cautioned that more data is needed to confirm the trend. Core CPI rose 0.3% in October, the third straight month of stronger-than-expected readings. Citi now expects core PCE inflation, the Fed’s preferred gauge, to rise to 3.2% year over year in October. “Some details of October data may offer the clearest signs yet that higher input and transportation costs are pushing up other prices,” the bank wrote. October showed unusually large increases in household furnishings, restaurants, medical goods, car insurance and local transport such as taxis. Citi said higher taxi fares very likely reflect gas prices, while stronger furnishings prices may reflect higher shipping costs. “But we also remain cautious that data has been much more volatile than usual, and more months of data will be needed to judge the degree of pass through,” Citi said. The bank noted that core CPI was flat as recently as June. It also warned that annual inflation readings for October and November will be distorted upward by last year’s government shutdown, before normalizing with December data. Citi expects the next four months of inflation data to be strong, though it sees downside risks to high expectations in the first quarter. Factors that boosted early 2026 inflation, such as airfares, may be weaker this time. “If rising prices do reflect more energy price pass-through, we would expect some stickiness to stronger increases, with prices continuing to rise over the next few months,” the bank added.

items.title: US retail sales increase moderately; import prices rise above expectations By Reuters
items.excerpt: WASHINGTON, Nov 17 (Reuters) - US retail sales increased moderately in October as households pulled back on purchases of motor vehicles and furniture, but maintained spending elsewhere, keeping the economy on solid footing at the start of the fourth quarter. The report from the Commerce Department on Tuesday also showed upward revisions to September sales. Spending has remained resilient despite rising inflation pressuring household budgets. The underlying strength in retail sales, together with other data on Tuesday showing a bigger-than-expected increase in import prices last month, reinforced economists’ views that the Federal Reserve would continue raising ​interest rates after next month’s widely expected hike. "More consumers ‌are clearly struggling with rapidly rising prices but are not yet ready to throw in the towel," said Scott ​Anderson, chief US economist at BMO Capital Markets. "Instead, consumers appear to be strategically allocating their monthly budgets to stretch their dollars into different categories every month. While under some pressure, real consumer spending is expected to perform well enough in the fourth quarter to ‌keep the Fed focused on its inflation mandate." Retail sales rose 0.2% last month after an unrevised ⁠0.8% surge in September, the Commerce Department’s Census Bureau said. The increase was in ​line with economists’ expectations. Retail sales are mostly goods and are not adjusted for inflation. They gained 6.8% on a year-on-year basis in October. The ongoing US-Israeli war with Iran is driving up inflation, eroding households’ purchasing power. The government reported last month that income at the disposal of households after adjusting for inflation and taxes fell 0.3% in September. Consumer spending is being driven mostly by higher-income households, which have been cushioned against inflation by stock market gains. But the recent technology-led selloff could temper spending by making consumers more cautious. Economists have also noted a reliance on credit ‌cards by more households, with money from generous tax refunds earlier in the year exhausted. Households are also saving less and dipping into their nest eggs to afford purchases. The saving rate fell to a near four-year low in September. Retail sales over the month were held back by a 1.6% decline in receipts at auto dealers. Sales at ‌furniture retailers fell 2.3%, while receipts at electronics and appliance stores were unchanged. There were decreases in sales at clothing retailers ‌as well as at sporting goods, hobby, musical instrument and book stores. But building material store sales increased 0.5%. ‌Sales at nonstore retailers jumped 1.2%. Receipts at food services and drinking places rose 0.2%. UNDERLYING STRENGTH IN RETAIL SALES Retail sales excluding automobiles, gasoline, building materials and food services increased 0.6% last month after an upwardly revised 0.5% rise ‌in ‌September. Economists had forecast these so-called core retail sales, which correspond most closely with the consumer spending component of gross domestic product, advancing 0.4% after a previously reported 0.1% gain in September. Consumer spending increased at a 3.8% annualized rate in the third quarter. The economy grew at a 3.4% pace in the July-September ⁠quarter. ... Import prices were last month driven by a 3.6% rise in the cost of fuels. That followed a ‌6.3% jump in September. There were ... Imported food prices fell 0.2% after rising 0.4% in September.

items.title: Fed’s Williams still favors tighter monetary policy, but says now is not the time for ’dramatic action’ By Reuters
items.excerpt: NEW YORK, Nov 17 (Reuters) - Federal Reserve Bank of New York President John Williams said on Tuesday the US central bank will likely need to raise rates again to lean against high inflation but he pushed back against the idea the Fed needs to shift to a more aggressive path of action. While inflation is too high and has been stubborn, there is not a need for “dramatic action” on the part of monetary policy, Williams said at the Axios BFD Annual Summit in New York. “I think what we’ve been doing over the last, past few months … is working well,” Williams said, adding, “We still have our work to do to make sure that we bring inflation back down to 2% in a timely way and in a sustained manner.” Williams said that recent data is clearly showing that “the economy remains resilient” and the jobs market is “solid,” while “inflation, unfortunately, is not moving in the right direction.” The Fed’s interest-rate-setting Federal Open Market Committee is next scheduled to meet over December 8 and 9 in a gathering traders and investors broadly expect to result in a quarter-percentage-point increase in what is now a 3.75% to 4% federal funds target rate range. If the Fed delivers that hike, it will be the second of the year. Markets are expecting to see at least another increase next year as well. The Fed has been raising rates to combat high levels of inflation, and a number of officials have noted in recent weeks that price pressures have been getting worse rather than better. Many have made the case for a gradual path of rate rises, which they argue allows the economy to adjust to higher borrowing costs.

items.excerpt: ## Schumer says he has votes to become Senate majority leader Sen. Chuck Schumer said Tuesday that he has locked down the votes to be elected Senate majority leader and called his race against Sen. Chris Van Hollen effectively over. Schumer urged Democrats to focus on lowering costs and ending corruption, and said the caucus is united. items.excerpt: ## Trump Arrives in Philippines Ahead of ASEAN Summit and Meeting with Putin, Xi Nov 17, 2026 President Trump has arrived in the Philippines on the first leg of a 48-hour trip to Asia. He’s scheduled to meet with President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. ahead of the ASEAN summit of Southeast Asian nations. Trump’s visit has drawn large protests in Manila, where police arrested hundreds of people over the weekend. Students, workers and progressive groups are demanding an end to the U.S. and Israeli war on Iran and are protesting against plans to build an artificial intelligence and manufacturing hub near Manila. On Thursday, Trump will hold an unprecedented trilateral summit in Shenzhen, China, with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin. Trump also said he might meet with North Korean leader Kim Jong-un while in China. ... The Trump administration ... ## Trump Takes “No Responsibility” for Largest FAA Ground Stop Since 9/11 Nov 17, 2026 United Airlines canceled dozens of departing flights and delayed more than 800 others on Monday after a system outage that lasted more than 90 minutes. United blamed a “technical issue,” without elaborating, and said in a statement there was “no indication that this was a cybersecurity-related issue.” This comes after the FAA ordered a nearly five-hour nationwide ground stop on Friday, causing over 18,000 flight cancellations and more than 28,000 delays. It was the largest disruption of its kind to U.S. air travel since the 9/11 attacks. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy is due to brief senators about the incident today. On Monday, President Trump said Duffy had his full support, and blamed the Biden administration for the grounded flights. ... ## Largest Union of U.S. Nurses Endorses Sen. Van Hollen for Senate Majority Leader The largest union of nurses in the United States has endorsed Maryland’s Chris Van Hollen to lead the Senate Democratic caucus when the new Congress begins in January. In a statement, National Nurses United wrote, “The Democratic Party must not squander the chance midterm voters have given it to tackle our nation in crisis. Nurses and working people demand new Senate leadership that confronts the billionaire class, corporations, and governments to deliver transformative change for us. Sen. Van Hollen is the best person for the job.” The endorsement came after Van Hollen said he had a path to defeat New York Senator Chuck Schumer in a contested leadership challenge. Van Hollen was interviewed on CNN’s “State of the Union” on Sunday. > Sen. Chris Van Hollen: “This is not about one person or any one individual. This really is a response to the call of the voters, who clearly rejected Donald Trump and his awful policies. But they haven’t fully hired the Democrats. They’ve given us a chance, and I think we need to earn their trust. And I think that begins by not going back to business as usual, not going back to the status quo.” Meanwhile, Senator Van Hollen told Politico he supports New York Congressmember Hakeem Jeffries for House speaker.

Dave Mustaine and company will stop at Mystic Lake Amphitheater in Shakopee on May 29. ... ### Taylor Swift Sets New Grammy Record With 5 Years of Major-Category Nominations (Billboard) Taylor Swift has set a new Grammy record with yesterday’s nominations. She is up for album, record, and song of the year in the same year for the fifth time. This makes her the new record holder for the most times any artist has been nominated in the big three all-genre categories in the same year. Swift is also nominated for best pop duo/group performance for her “The Life of a Showgirl” duet with Sabrina Carpenter and is nominated for best song written for visual media for Toy Story 5’s “I Knew It, I Knew You,” which she co-wrote with Jack Antonoff. Taylor Swift is sitting at 63 nominations and 14 wins total for her career so far. ... Beyoncé became the first artist in history to land 100 lifetime Grammy nominations when her B’Day 20th anniversary reissue bonus track, “Morning Dew (Donk),” picked up a nod for best R&B solo performance. The song was released on July 4 and was written by Beyoncé, Pharrell Williams, The-Dream, and Darius Dixon and produced by Beyoncé and Pharrell. Beyoncé is already the artist with the most Grammys – she has 35 total. We’ll see if she adds another to the shelf during the awards in February.

items.excerpt: ## 1. Six Nigerians on the 2027 Grammy list ### What happened The Recording Academy announced nominations for the 69th Grammy Awards on Monday. Nigerian acts hold four of the five spots in Best African Music Performance: Asake twice, for Gratitude and for Jogodo with Wizkid, Tems for Big Daddy, and Ayra Starr with Beninese singer Angélique Kidjo for Aye Kan (Are You Coming Back?). The fifth nominee is Ghana’s King Ayisoba with Rocky Dawuni. Three Nigerian albums are up for Best Global Music Album: Tems’ Love Is a Kingdom, Davido’s Oriadé and Ayra Starr’s Starrgirl. Burna Boy is nominated in Best Global Music Performance for Dai Dai, his World Cup song with Shakira. Tems also picked up R&B recognition for What You Need. Outlets count her total differently, with some listing three nominations and others four, because she appears as a songwriter in Best R&B Song as well as a performer. ### Why it matters Nigerian artists are now competing with each other for the same trophy, which says a lot about how far the sound has travelled. The ceremony is on 7 February 2027 at the Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles and will air on ABC and stream on Disney+ and Hulu. For background, see our ranking of the best Afrobeats albums of 2026. Source: ThisDay; TVC News; Peoples Gazette. ## 2. AMAA 2026: Kenya and Côte d’Ivoire lead, Nigeria picks up key prizes ### What happened The 22nd Africa Movie Academy Awards held on Sunday night at the Marriott Hotel in Ikeja, Lagos. One Woman One Bra, a Kenya-Nigeria co-production directed by Vincho Nchogu, won Best Film, Best Film in an African Language and Best Debut Feature. The Colour of Exile from Côte d’Ivoire won the most awards, four, including Best Director and Best Actress for Naky Sy Savane. Nigeria’s main winners were Wale Ojo (Best Actor, Lights Out), Linda Ejiofor (Best Supporting Actress, The Herd) and To Adaego With Love, which took Best Nigerian Film and the screenplay award. The Herd also won for production design and make-up, The Creek for visual effects, and Evi for soundtrack. ### Why it matters Nollywood still dominated the nomination lists, but the top prizes went elsewhere this year, a reminder that the rest of the continent’s film industry is growing fast too. Source: Channels TV; TheCable Lifestyle; Afrocritik. ## 3. Box office: Five Figurines on top, Agbara Nla keeps climbing ### Five Figurines and Issakaba Returns Akay Mason’s thriller Five Figurines, starring Bimbo Akintola and Odunlade Adekola, opened at number one over the 13 to 15 November weekend. Its distributors put the takings at more than ₦64.8 million and called it the biggest November opening for a Nollywood film. Industry tracker Fusion Intelligence reports about ₦64.4 million from 9,789 admissions, around 30 per cent of the weekend’s total, with Sunday alone bringing in ₦33.1 million. Issakaba Returns opened second with ₦44 million, or ₦46.5 million including previews. ### Agbara Nla: The Return passes ₦513 million Distributor Nile Entertainment said on Monday that the remake of Mike Bamiloye’s 1993 Christian classic has now made more than ₦513.4 million since it opened on 1 October. That makes it the second-biggest Nollywood film of 2026 behind Call of My Life, and the ninth-biggest Nollywood title ever. ### Why it matters Two Nollywood films opening above ₦40 million in the same weekend, outside the December rush, is a good sign for cinemas heading into the festive season. Source: QED; Fusion Intelligence; Punch. ## 4. Olamide drops Time and Space ### What happened Olamide released Time and Space on Monday through YBNL Nation and EMPIRE. It has 10 songs and runs about 32 minutes. FOLA is the only guest, on Jaiye, and October’s single Burukutu sits at track four. Olamide said he painted the cover art himself. The album follows his self-titled 2025 record, Olamidé, which had a much longer guest list.
